source_review.excerpt:
4.2.1       Height of the ice load area

An ice-strengthened ship is assumed to operate in open sea conditions corresponding to a level
ice thickness not exceeding hi. The design ice load height (h) of the area actually under ice
pressure at any particular point of time is, however, assumed to be only a fraction of the ice
thickness. The values for hi and h are given in Table 4-1.

                     Table 4-1: Values of hi and h for the different ice classes
                             Ice Class           hi [m]           h [m]
                             IA Super               1.0            0.35
                             IA                     0.8            0.30
                             IB                     0.6            0.25
                             IC                     0.4            0.22


4.2.2       Ice pressure

The design ice pressure is determined by the formula:

                                      𝑝𝑝 = 𝑐𝑐𝑑𝑑 𝑐𝑐𝑝𝑝 𝑐𝑐𝑎𝑎 𝑝𝑝0 [MPa],                            (4.1)
source_review.review_note: All four Table4-1 hi/h cells reviewed: IA Super1/.35, IA .8/.30, IB .6/.25, IC .4/.22.

queries:
PREFIX nltl: <https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#>
            PREFIX qudt: <http://qudt.org/schema/qudt/>
            PREFIX unit: <http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/>
            PREFIX sh: <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#>
            PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>

            SELECT $this
            WHERE {
                ?ship nltl:hasIceClassDesignParameterSet $this ;
                       nltl:iceClass ?class .
                $this nltl:levelIceThickness ?hiQuantity ;
                      nltl:designIceLoadHeight ?hQuantity .
                ?hiQuantity qudt:numericValue ?hi ;
                            qudt:unit unit:M .
                ?hQuantity qudt:numericValue ?h ;
                           qudt:unit unit:M .
                FILTER (
                    (?class = nltl:iceClassIaSuper &&
                     (?hi > 1.0 || ?h != 0.35)) ||
                    (?class = nltl:iceClassIa &&
                     (?hi > 0.8 || ?h != 0.30)) ||
                    (?class = nltl:iceClassIb &&
                     (?hi > 0.6 || ?h != 0.25)) ||
                    (?class = nltl:iceClassIc &&
                     (?hi > 0.4 || ?h != 0.22))
                )
            }
